steps: Open the public entry page.
Browse coding challenges by track.
Filter challenges by difficulty, topic, status, or success rate.
Open a challenge and inspect its problem, examples, constraints, and starter code.
Register a local learner account with the required identity fields.
Read the local verification message and verify the account.
Complete the basic profile.
Sign out and sign back in with local credentials.
Choose a programming language and edit the solution.
Run the draft against deterministic sample or custom input.
Inspect stdout, errors, and test results.
Submit the solution and inspect its status, runtime, memory, and failed-case feedback.
Open challenge submission history.
Inspect a previous submission and its source.
Load the source into the editor.
Edit and resubmit it as a new version.
Open the discussion page for a challenge.
Read seeded official guidance and community explanations.
Return to the problem without posting to HackerRank.
Save a challenge.
Open the dashboard.
Review local progress, streak, badges, learning plans, and newest activity.
Open the newest activity item and return to its challenge.
Browse seeded contests and assessments.
Open profile and settings.
Update the local bio, preferred language, and notification choices.
Verify the changes persist after navigation.
Apply the impossible search zzzz-no-match-websitebench and observe a no-results message.
Submit a required challenge action while signed out and observe a sign-in prompt.
Submit required account fields empty and observe inline guidance.
Open a missing deep link and return safely to challenge discovery.
Open password recovery and inspect the email field and validation guidance.
Submit a local account address.
Use the local-only verification message to replace the password.
Return to sign-in without contacting a real mail provider.
Open support.
Find guidance for challenge discovery, account access, and failed runs or submissions.
Return to practice without exposing private account data.
